relationships.description: The model-wide coverage report tallies each coverage requirement of its model in its requirement totals, and the requirement exists independently of any particular report snapshot.
relationships.evidence: The generated summary record lists or counts the requirement's identifier among its totalled requirements, and that identifier matches a requirement defined in the same coverage model file.

relationships.description: The model-wide report rolls up the per-target coverage records of its model, using their designed, implemented and automated counts to compute the overall figures.
relationships.evidence: The summary's per-target section embeds or links the target summary records, and its totals equal the sum of those records' counts in the same report run.

relationships.description: The model-wide report counts each test case sketch of the model in its designed, implemented and automated totals without owning the sketch's lifecycle.
relationships.evidence: The summary's sketch totals are computed from the sketch entries in the coverage model, and the report lists the sketch identifiers or their implementation status.

relationships.description: The report presents the coverage model as the whole whose contents it totals, treating the model as a captured part of the point-in-time snapshot.
relationships.evidence: The summary record embeds a snapshot or version-pinned copy of the coverage model it was generated from.

relationships.description: The report cannot be computed without the model's coverage targets, since every per-target figure and overall target count is derived from them.
relationships.evidence: The report generator iterates over the model's declared targets to compute totals, and a summary with no targets fails generation or reports zero scope.

relationships.description: The report provides the evidence demanded by a motivation requirement that mandates reported test coverage, such as a requirement to publish coverage before release.
relationships.evidence: The requirement's acceptance criteria cite the coverage summary report, and the release checklist or traceability matrix links the summary record as satisfying evidence.

relationships.description: The report's totals serve as the measured value showing whether a stated coverage outcome, such as 90% of requirements exercised, has been reached.
relationships.evidence: The outcome's target value names a summary metric, and a dashboard or quality gate compares the summary's computed percentage to that threshold.

relationships.description: The report cites a business process whose workflow targets it totals, so readers can see coverage status in terms of that process.
relationships.evidence: The summary record includes the business process identifier in a scope or grouping field, matching a business-workflow target in the model.

relationships.description: The report cites the approved exclusions that remove targets or requirements from its required-coverage denominator, so that excluded items are not counted as shortfalls.
relationships.evidence: The summary lists exclusion identifiers in an excluded-items section, and its required-coverage denominator is reduced by exactly those excluded items.

relationships.description: The report points to the recorded coverage gaps that explain why its exercised share falls short of required coverage.
relationships.evidence: The summary contains links or identifiers of open gap records, and each referenced gap names a requirement or target counted as unexercised in the totals.

relationships.description: The report identifies the single coverage model and version whose contents it summarises at its snapshot time.
relationships.evidence: The summary record carries a model identifier and version field that resolves to an existing coverage model definition.

relationships.description: The report gives the coverage model's owners a consolidated status view that they use to track the test plan's progress.
relationships.evidence: The coverage model's documentation or CI pipeline publishes the summary as its status report, for example as a build artifact attached to the model's repository.

relationships.description: The report states whether each coverage requirement has been exercised by at least one implemented test, confirming or refuting that the criterion is met.
relationships.evidence: The summary marks each requirement identifier as exercised or not, based on links from implemented test functions to the sketches for that requirement.

notes: aggregates→TestCoverageModel inverts the containment: the model is reported on, not part of the report; with references and serves to the same model, three predicates express one link—keep references. validates→CoverageRequirement overstates a report's role; it reports status rather than performing verification. fulfills-requirements→Requirement is weak for a report record.
